reasons: technical: The image that proves the cross-node join shows a trace with an unexplained missing parent. With propagation on, the orders server span names parent e76355175e7d3f75, which is not among the trace's spans. The load client sends a random traceparent on every request but never logs it, so the lab cannot tell whether OBI adopted the caller's context once headers propagation was on. If it did, Splunk APM will show these traces with a missing root whenever a caller sends traceparent. A reader turning on the second value needs to know this, and finding out is cheap. Fix: In the propagation round, have load.py log each sent traceparent (trace ID and span ID) and compare it with the 30 sampled traces. Report how many orders server spans have a parent from the load client, and how many come from OBI's span for `load`. Or run one more propagation round with the traceparent header removed. Then replace the 'doesn't show whose it is' sentence with the measured answer.
outside claim without a known source: OBI's Java agent is on by default, provides TLS tracing, virtual-thread correlation and runtime metrics, and javaagent.enabled turns it off
outside claim without a known source: Service discovery settings can narrow what OBI instruments, including by namespace
outside claim without a known source: Splunk describes an inferred service as one it deduces from a caller's span

Every headline number matches a corroborated contract line: 2 of 2 services sent their own spans, all 3 pods kept their UIDs with 0 restarts after each value, 0 of 30 traces joined with the default and 30 of 30 with propagation, and the effective privileges were captured.

The post's claims stay within the evidence. It says outright that the libinstrument mappings do not show the attach finished, that the cause of orders inferred=true is unknown, and that the 2.58 ms median p95 difference sits inside a 7.58 ms OFF spread. It does not call that difference zero overhead.

The proof trace leaves an open question. With propagation on, the orders server span has a parent (e76355175e7d3f75) that is not in the trace. The load client sends a random traceparent on every request but never logs it, so the lab cannot say whether OBI took up the caller's context. Readers whose callers already send traceparent need that answer.

The post says 'CPU on the orders node read 8 to 11 percent', but load.py reads /proc/stat on the node the load pod runs on. The lib.sh round helper that would show per-node CPU is cut off in the material I have, so I can't verify which node that number comes from.
One clear reader with one decision. The title delivers what it promises, and the opening gives the result straight away: 2 services, 0 restarts, 30 of 30 joined.

The real finding goes beyond the docs. The map draws orders -> inventory from the first value alone, but 0 of 30 traces cross nodes until propagation is on. That split is useful for planning, and only measurement shows it.
Trade-offs are handled honestly and kept in the body (privileges, namespace scope, Java agent, latency). Credit stays positive and goes to the Splunk chart and OBI.

Some sentences read stiffly and in an even rhythm ('This run doesn't show why the flag is set, so I report both facts and no cause.'). Two loose ends are disclosed rather than resolved: why orders is inferred, and whose span the foreign parent is. Those are the questions a sharp reader will ask first.

Demand evidence is weak: one OBI GitHub issue (#3895) with a few comments. That issue is about Java agent injection under reduced capabilities, not about getting a first map without restarts. No search volume data was provided.

The headline uses product wording ('One Helm Value', 'Splunk APM Map'). There is no evidence that it matches how readers phrase the problem, such as 'trace without restarting pods' or 'eBPF tracing EKS Java'.
Splunk fits naturally, and the reader is well chosen. I can't justify a higher score without a linked signal such as reactions, comments or views.

claims.text: OBI is a beta feature in Splunk Observability Cloud and runs as a DaemonSet capturing traces and request metrics from outside the process
OBI's Java agent is on by default, provides TLS tracing, virtual-thread correlation and runtime metrics, and javaagent.enabled turns it off
OBI's outgoing propagation is off by default
Proxies and load balancers can affect propagation
Async frameworks need their own check for context propagation
Service discovery settings can narrow what OBI instruments, including by namespace
Splunk describes an inferred service as one it deduces from a caller's span
Privileged, host PID and host network are the chart's defaults, the guide covers reduced permissions, and it names Ubuntu as its tested OS
Splunk recommends combining OBI with language agents
Non-root JVMs need attention when OBI's capabilities are reduced
Language agents give the deepest detail and join the JVM at startup, so pods have to roll
Chart 0.164.0 ships the same OBI version as 0.163.1 (README)

brief.reader: Platform engineer running Java services on EKS who wants a first service map before asking any team to change a deployment
brief.decision: Whether to turn on OBI through the Splunk OTel Collector chart as a first layer across a cluster, before rolling out language agents
brief.question: Can I get services that are already running on EKS onto the Splunk APM map without restarting a pod, and what do I get from it?
brief.takeaway: You can decide from measured numbers: what one Helm value puts on the map for running services, what it does to the pods, and whether traces across nodes need a second value.
brief.adds: Existing pages state that OBI needs no restart and list what it captures. This post measures it on EKS on Amazon Linux 2023: services on the map, each pod's UID and restart count before and after, whether one trace spans two nodes with and without propagation, the Java helper OBI loads, and the p95 latency added.
brief.open_question: With obi.enabled=true alone on chart 0.163.1, how many running services reach the Splunk APM map, how many pod restarts does it add, and how many services share one trace across two nodes with and without outgoing header propagation?
tradeoffs: OBI first for a broad map, or a language agent for deeper framework detail
A privileged DaemonSet with host PID and host network, or the chart's documented reduced capabilities
Every namespace by default, or a namespace filter
Outgoing header propagation on, or kept at its default
